View of a severed hand and foot skewered and hung from a tree; identified as having belonged to a chief of the village of Mongtikung (or Montikong, now Mongtikang), probably Gaonbura, and as being located in the Ao Naga village of Yacham (now Yachem).

View, slightly from the side, of six carved wooden human figures of leading men and women of Mongsenyimti [Mongsemdi] made by people of Chuchuyimlang [Susu] for sympathetic magic, against an outside wall.

Full-length portrait of an Ao Naga man possibly named Yaripala, wearing horn-shaped necklaces, wrist ornaments, a European-style waistcoat, and a woven apron, holding a spear and a dao (cutting implement) with a tassel.
'2 women of Ungma / Ao.' (handwritten caption). Half-length portrait of two Ao Naga women of Ungma, carrying large baskets on their backs, with a third woman in the background.
'Aos fishing in the DIKHU'  (handwritten caption). View from across the river of several dozen Ao Naga people fishing in the shallows of the Dikhu river.
'Aos fishing in the Dikhu' (handwritten caption). View from across the river of several dozen Ao Naga people clustered on the bank of the Dikhu river to fish.
Full-length portrait of an Ao Naga man identified as NinaNioran, wearing a necklace and wrapped in a cloak with a woven pattern, with three other people in the background.
View from middle distance of several dozen Ao Naga people fishing in the shallows of the Dikhu river, with a weir or trap constructed in the river.
View from across the river of several dozen Ao Naga people clustered on the bank of the Dikhu river to fish.

View of stones amid vegetation at the village of Lungtrok (now Longtrok), 'from which [stones] all the Aos derive their origin, as well as the Phoms and, I think, Sangtams hereabouts' (J. H. Hutton, Diaries of Two Tours).

View of a 'female' stone amid vegetation at the village of Lungtrok (now Longtrok), one of the six stones there 'from which all the Aos derive their origin, as well as the Phoms and, I think, Sangtams hereabouts' (J. H. Hutton, Diaries of Two Tours).
View of a dead bear, with its mouth wide open, attached to a wooden or bamboo frame, at Chuchuyimlang [Susu].
View of a dead bear and another animal, both attached to a wooden or bamboo frame, with a group of six Ao Naga men standing behind it, at Chuchuyimlang [Susu].
View of an Ao Naga man named Ta[i]ongnokelü of Salulamang, dancing with a spear, facing the photographer.
View of an Ao Naga man named Ta[i]ongnokelü of Salulamang, dancing with a spear, with head down, beneath a tree.
View from across the river of several dozen Ao Naga people fishing in the shallows of the Dikhu river.

View of two decorated pillars, one of them with a carving of a leopard, and a wall panel decorated with a four-limbed figure, at the entrance to an Ao Naga morung (house for unmarried men) in Changtongya [Chantungia].
